_why: The rendered 'Current site state' line, as a table BOTH suites assert against.
The line is produced twice, in two languages: docker/chat/app/site_state.py renders it
into the system instruction, and js/site-state-notes.js renders it into the live
clientContent note (ADR-0015 §7). A live voice session therefore hears the same fact in
two voices, and if they drift it hears two DIFFERENT facts about the same site — the
model has no way to tell which is current.
This file exists because that exact drift has already cost this project four months:
providers.py and live_gemini.py each declared navigate_to_section with its own section
enum, they diverged, and the voice model could not emit `labs` at all (ADR-0015 §9.3).
The fix there was a test asserting the two declarations are EQUAL. This is the same
move, made before the drift rather than after it: one table, two readers, and neither
renderer can change alone.
Each case is the WIRE shape (§6.1) and the line it must render to. A renderer that
cannot produce a row fails its own suite; it cannot quietly disagree with the other one.
voiceActive IS on the wire but is NOT rendered into the prose. On the live path the
model IS the voice session, so saying it is a tautology that costs a clause in every
note; on the text path the composer's modes are mutually exclusive, so it is never true
there. It stays on the wire because it is worth persisting on the turn (6.4) - the
admin panel wants to know a failed turn happened during a call.
The rows below with no section exist because the first version of both renderers
produced "the visitor is with the contact form open." - a sentence with no complement.
Reachable: the store accepts any non-empty section string, and the wire producer NULLS
one whose shape the server would refuse, so section can legitimately arrive as null with
the rest of the state intact. And a project title containing a double quote nested inside
the quotes the line puts around it, which reads to the model as a broken delimiter.
Neither renderer was pinned on either case; the table is the contract, so they go here.
